checkpoints.question: Which of the following best describes smishing and why it is effective as a threat vector?

options.A: Smishing is phishing via email attachments; it carries malicious links that lead to credential-harvesting pages
options.B: Smishing is phishing via SMS text message; small screens make URL inspection difficult and texts feel urgent
options.C: Smishing is phishing via social media; it enables attackers to build fake profiles and gather personal details
options.D: Smishing is phishing via instant messaging platforms; it allows attackers to impersonate colleagues and appear trustworthy

checkpoints.explanation: The section explicitly defines smishing as phishing via SMS text message and identifies two reasons it is effective: small screens make URL inspection hard and texts feel urgent. The other options describe different threat vectors or communication channels.

checkpoints.question: What is steganography and how does it function as an attack vector?

options.A: Steganography is an XML-based image format containing embedded JavaScript used to enable cross-site scripting attacks on web browsers
options.B: Steganography creates files that are simultaneously valid images and valid executable code, confusing format parsers during processing
options.C: Steganography exploits rendering vulnerabilities in image file handlers to inject malicious scripts into web content served to users
options.D: Steganography hides data or malicious code inside image files to conceal payloads and exfiltrate information without detection

checkpoints.explanation: The section defines steganography as hiding data or malicious code inside an image file invisibly to conceal payloads or exfiltrate data. The other options describe SVG files, polyglot files, and XSS vulnerabilities respectively.

checkpoints.question: Which file type is capable of executing arbitrary commands when opened and has been used in sophisticated APT campaigns?

options.A: LNK files, which are Windows shortcut files that can be crafted to execute arbitrary commands when opened
options.B: PDF files that can contain embedded JavaScript or exploit vulnerabilities in PDF reader software
options.C: ZIP archives that hide malicious files among hundreds of legitimate ones to evade detection
options.D: VBA macros embedded in Microsoft Office documents that automate tasks when users enable them

checkpoints.explanation: The section specifically identifies LNK files as Windows shortcut files that can execute arbitrary commands when opened and notes their use in sophisticated APT campaigns. While other file types listed are vectors, only LNK files are explicitly connected to APT usage.

checkpoints.question: What is vishing and what technique does an attacker use to make calls appear to come from a trusted source?

options.A: Vishing is automated spam delivered over IP networks using recorded social engineering scripts dialed to large numbers of targets
options.B: Vishing is war dialing that systematically calls phone number ranges to locate active modems and identify exploitable network systems
options.C: Vishing is voice phishing where attackers impersonate trusted entities via phone calls and use caller ID spoofing through VoIP systems
options.D: Vishing exploits VoIP vulnerabilities to intercept phone calls and extract sensitive credentials from voice conversations and call audio

checkpoints.explanation: The section defines vishing as voice phishing where attackers impersonate trusted entities like banks or IT support, and identifies caller ID spoofing via VoIP as the technique used to appear legitimate. The other options describe SPIT, war dialing, and a different VoIP-related concept.

checkpoints.question: How does HID emulation function as a removable media threat vector?

options.A: HID emulation devices disguise themselves as keyboards to the OS, bypassing software controls and executing pre-programmed malicious keystrokes
options.B: HID emulation devices allow insiders to copy sensitive data to a thumb drive and physically remove it from the network
options.C: HID emulation devices intercept traffic and harvest credentials through malicious code hidden inside removable media files
options.D: HID emulation devices scatter USB drives in parking lots hoping employees will plug them in and trigger auto-executing malware

checkpoints.explanation: The section explains that HID emulation devices like the USB Rubber Ducky appear as trusted keyboards to the OS, then execute hundreds of pre-programmed malicious keystrokes per second, bypassing software controls. The other options describe baiting, data exfiltration, and a different threat vector.

checkpoints.question: What is the key vulnerability of unsupported systems that have reached end-of-life status?

options.A: Unsupported systems can be compromised through software backdoors inserted during the build or update delivery process
options.B: Unsupported systems are permanently vulnerable because the vendor releases no more security patches once EOL is reached
options.C: Unsupported systems are high-value targets because compromising the server affects every user session at once
options.D: Unsupported systems are vulnerable to exploit kits that automatically test for known vulnerabilities in browsers and readers

checkpoints.explanation: The section explicitly states that unsupported systems past end-of-life have no more security patches released by the vendor, making them permanently vulnerable. The other options describe exploit kits, the threat level of web applications, and supply chain attacks respectively.

checkpoints.question: What weakness makes WEP unsuitable as a wireless encryption standard?

options.A: WEP is an old protocol that provides no encryption at all, allowing nearby attackers to passively sniff all traffic
options.B: WEP is vulnerable to evil twin access points that mimic legitimate network names and intercept user connections
options.C: WEP has cryptographic weaknesses that allow key recovery in minutes, making it now-broken and unsuitable
options.D: WEP lacks port-based network authentication and cannot verify user identity before granting network access

checkpoints.explanation: The section specifically identifies WEP as an old, now-broken wireless encryption protocol with cryptographic weaknesses that allow key recovery in minutes. The other options describe open Wi-Fi, evil twin attacks, and 802.1X authentication respectively.

checkpoints.question: What is Shodan and how do attackers use it as a reconnaissance tool?

options.A: Shodan is a public database of default credentials that attackers combine with network scanning to achieve administrative system access
options.B: Shodan is a vulnerability assessment platform that tests internet-connected devices for known exploits and reports on their security
options.C: Shodan is a port scanning tool that detects open service ports and identifies vulnerable network protocols on connected systems
options.D: Shodan is an internet search engine indexing connected devices and their services; attackers use it to locate vulnerable software versions

checkpoints.explanation: The section defines Shodan as an internet search engine that indexes internet-connected devices and their exposed services, and states that attackers use it to find vulnerable software versions. The other options describe credential databases, port scanning tools, and vulnerability assessment platforms respectively.

checkpoints.question: What is a software backdoor supply chain attack and which real-world example is cited in the section?

options.A: A software backdoor supply chain attack adds malicious components during hardware manufacturing; the Cisco counterfeit switches case demonstrates this
options.B: A software backdoor supply chain attack targets managed service providers whose broad network access enables attackers to perform lateral movement
options.C: A software backdoor supply chain attack compromises build systems to inject malware into legitimate updates; SolarWinds Orion 2020 exemplifies this
options.D: A software backdoor supply chain attack exploits third-party contractor access to networks and pivots into point-of-sale systems like the 2013 Target incident

checkpoints.explanation: The section defines software backdoors as compromising build systems so malware is inserted into legitimate software updates delivered to customers, and specifically names the SolarWinds Orion 2020 attack as an example. The other options describe hardware tampering, MSP targeting, and the Target/HVAC contractor breach respectively.

checkpoints.question: How do attackers use social media platforms as a threat vector?

options.A: Attackers mine social media to identify employees, map organizational structure, and gather personal details that support spear-phishing campaigns
options.B: Attackers leverage social media to conduct caller ID spoofing and deliver voice phishing scripts to target employees at scale
options.C: Attackers use social media to distribute malicious links that trigger exploit kits when clicked by unsuspecting users
options.D: Attackers post fake profiles on social media to impersonate colleagues and distribute malicious files via instant messaging platforms

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that attackers mine LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter to identify employees, map organizational structure, and gather personal details that make spear-phishing convincing. The other options describe different attack vectors not specific to social media reconnaissance.
